display.title: Episode 158: The Three Loaves of Bread
display.summary_short: Why the Torah says 'es' when it commands us to honor parents, a whole family visits Studio 604, and King Shlomo solves the mystery of a widow's third loaf of bread.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens with simcha, the place where Hashem's presence rests, and everyone joins the Hakochainik march, followed by the sponsor's cheese commercial. At Mitzvah Time he asks why the Torah adds the word 'es' in 'kabed es avicha v'es imecha': the Sages learn from it that we must also honor an older brother or sister, and anyone older than us, for example by letting them go first or start eating first. A caller, wished a happy birthday, wins by sharing her own ways of honoring her father on Shabbos. Last week's winner then leads the Shema in the studio with her family. The story: an old woman gives two of her three fresh loaves to starving beggars, and then the wind blows the third loaf away into the sea. She asks King Shlomo why Hashem did this. While she eats, a foreign king arrives: his ship sprang a leak, he vowed half his wealth to charity, and a loaf of bread plugged the hole. Shlomo HaMelech has the woman bake an identical loaf and awards her the vow. The show closes with a way to earn Tzivos Hashem points by sending in a Dvar Torah.
display.lesson: Everything Hashem does is for the good, and kindness to others is repaid in ways we cannot imagine.
